questions.question: Which request content type carries files in an upload?
questions.explanation: multipart/form-data splits one request into sections, and each section can hold a file or a text field.

questions.question: Which header tells the browser to save the response as a file instead of opening it?
questions.explanation: Content-Disposition with the value attachment asks the browser to download the body as a file.

questions.question: The lab app limits a file to 1 MB. A client uploads a 1.5 MB file. What status does it get?
questions.explanation: Tomcat stops the request when it passes the multipart limit and replies 413 before the controller runs.

questions.question: The upload endpoint allows only pdf, png and jpg. What does a client get when it uploads virus.exe?
questions.explanation: The controller checks the extension and throws ResponseStatusException with status 415.

questions.question: A controller saves uploads with Files.copy(in, root.resolve(file.getOriginalFilename())). What is the danger?
options: The file will always be empty
A name like ../../app.jar can write outside the upload folder
questions.explanation: The client controls the file name, so path parts such as ../ can escape the folder unless you generate your own name.
